state.background: Review the triage decision to retain P42-179 under Plan42 simplification principles. The exact callsite is tests/e2e/consumption-mobile-acceptance.e2e.spec.ts:147: `expect(chart).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })`, in the test that first opens the nominal legend, hides all series, checks the empty state, then reselects one series and verifies the bar returns. P42-179 is only this initial chart-container visibility/readiness check; it is distinct from P42-180/181 (zero bars/empty-state assertions) and P42-182 (reselection/returning bar). The component tests can verify DOM/state but cannot establish actual browser layout, SVG rendering, or async route readiness. This line checks visibility of the chart wrapper, not the SVG itself. The subsequent `summary.click()` has Playwright actionability waits, but the later visible SVG bar assertion occurs only after the legend interaction/reselection, so it does not establish pre-interaction bar readiness. An independent architecture review recommends retaining unless evidence shows a preceding/subsequent visible SVG bar makes this 15-second check redundant. The assertion ledger currently describes the test's broader browser behavior and maps state/aria/empty DOM to component candidates while retaining rendered SVG disappearance/reappearance in Playwright. No code/test changes were made for this triage decision and no tests are to be rerun.
acceptanceCriteria: Retain P42-179 only if it provides a useful browser-level pre-interaction readiness/visibility signal not supplied by component RTL or by later E2E assertions; judge the exact wrapper-visibility check rather than conflating it with the empty-state or reselect assertions.
Plan42 simplification removes redundant DOM-only assertions while retaining browser-specific rendered behavior and readiness evidence when the component tests cannot establish it.

The separate interaction and outcome contracts remain distinct: P42-180/181 check all-series-empty behavior; P42-182 checks actual reselect recovery; P42-179 checks the starting chart container before interaction.
A retain decision does not overclaim that chart-container visibility proves an SVG bar exists; the subsequent click's actionability behavior and SVG assertion timing are considered accurately.
The assertion ledger's destination/reason wording remains consistent with the retain decision or any needed evidence/correction is identified.
verification: Source at lines 139-161 shows chart visibility before summary click and empty-state actions; first visible bar assertion is after series reselection.
Assertion ledger row P42-179 identifies the callsite and separates component DOM/state from browser SVG disappearance/reappearance.
No implementation changes or test runs are part of this review.
